hero.caption: The Seven Layers
hero.title: AI Code Review
hero.tagline: Seven layers of review, for any agent harness
hero.figure: Each layer has holes; stack them so the holes do not line up.
hero.svgTitle: AI Code Review: seven layers of review, for any agent harness
hero.desc: Engraved plate of the swiss-cheese model. Seven upright slices, numbered I to VII, stand in a row. One defect passes through holes in slices I and II and is stopped at III, security that blocks, marked BLOCK; another passes four slices and is stopped at V, risk-scaled human approval. The legend names the seven layers: verify before the PR; AI review on every PR; security that blocks; blocking automated checks; risk-scaled human approval; merge queue and staged release; detect fast, roll back. Based on the Claude Code team’s review process at Anthropic.

section.head: Implemented here by

section.question: What could go wrong with this change, and which check catches it best?
section.guard: Less human review must never mean more reverts or incidents.
section.figure: A defect falls through the holes in I and II and is stopped at III.
section.svgTitle: The seven layers of code review, in section
section.desc: Engraved geological section of seven strata, one per layer of code review, numbered I to VII from the top: verify before the PR; AI review on every PR; security that blocks; blocking automated checks; risk-scaled human approval; merge queue and staged release; detect fast, roll back. Each stratum names what implements it in this repository. A defect falls through holes in strata I and II and is stopped at III, marked BLOCK. Side notes: per change, ask what could go wrong and which check catches it best; less human review must never mean more reverts or incidents.

pipeline.caption: The Review Pipeline
stations: Runs first; any BLOCK is final
Posted at 2 of 3 REAL; deep 3 of 3
First line is the count; ends “Round N of 3”
pipeline.figure: One run of the pr-review-process skill at standard depth.
pipeline.desc: Engraved flow of one run of the pr-review-process skill, left to right in eight stations: prepare (diff, PR intent, REVIEW.md); classify the tier (classifier, then a second opinion); the security engine runs first and any BLOCK is final, reported and stopped; bug hunters in fresh context and in parallel (quick 1, standard 3, deep 5); verifiers vote and a finding is posted at 2 of 3 REAL (deep 3 of 3); filter (style dropped, nitCap 3, labels Important, Nit, Pre-existing); report (first line is the count, ends Round N of 3); a human decides, and agent approvals never count.

tiers.caption: Risk Tiers
tiers.lead: The change sets the tier, not the author.
tiers: Docs, copy, internal-only code, additive behaviour behind a flag
0 human approvals, once AI review and security are green
Ordinary product changes; caching, auto-updater, system prompts
Billing, auth, migrations, and a small set of paths that always need two
rules: Highest path wins: one high path makes the whole PR high.
The second opinion can only raise the need for a person.
CI workflow files always need a person.
Agent and bot approvals are not human approvals.
Approvals are dismissed on new commits.
tiers.figure: Three tiers; each seal is one human approval.
tiers.desc: Engraved plate of three pedestals of rising height for the risk tiers. Low: docs, copy, internal-only code, additive behaviour behind a flag; 0 human approvals once AI review and security are green. Medium: ordinary product changes and sensitive areas such as caching, auto-updater and system prompts; 1 human approval. High: billing, auth, migrations and a small set of paths that always need two; 2 human approvals. Each approval is drawn as a seal. The change sets the tier, not the author. Rules: highest path wins; the second opinion can only raise the need for a person; CI workflow files always need a person; agent and bot approvals are not human approvals; approvals are dismissed on new commits.

convergence.caption: Convergence
convergence.problem: One PR ran 50+ overnight review rounds; about 59% of what was flagged had already been there on the first pass.
convergence.cap: After 3 rounds the reviewer stops listing and asks the author to reconsider the approach.
convergence.head: Reported results at the source
convergence.note: The originating team’s numbers on their own repos. Measure yours; do not assume them.
convergence.figure: Each round reviews only what changed; the cap is three.
convergence.svgTitle: Convergence: stop review that never ends
convergence.desc: Engraved plate on review convergence. A spiral closes in over round 1, round 2 and round 3 to the words reconsider the approach: after 3 rounds the reviewer stops listing and asks the author to reconsider the approach. The problem: one PR ran 50+ overnight review rounds, and about 59% of what was flagged had already been there on the first pass. Results reported at the source, before and after: PRs passing after one round, 65% to 78%; PRs needing 5+ rounds, 8.9% to 1.5%; mean reviews per PR, 2.08 to 1.32. These are the originating team’s numbers on their own repos.

harness.caption: Any Harness
harness.keyFull: Parallel subagents, each in fresh context
harness.keySeq: One role after another, context cleared between them
harness.same: Same in every harness: the voting rule (2 of 3; deep 3 of 3), the round cap of 3, the security BLOCK.
harness.figure: Each harness folder is a thin adapter; no role logic is duplicated.
harness.svgTitle: The review process in any harness
harness.desc: Engraved plate in the manner of an orrery. At the centre, a medallion: the review process, defined once in reviewers/*.md and SKILL.md. Six harnesses sit on the ring around it: claude-code runs the full process with parallel subagents in fresh context; kiro, codex, cursor, copilot and gemini run it sequentially, one role after another with context cleared between them. The same in every harness: the voting rule (2 of 3; deep 3 of 3), the round cap of 3 and the security BLOCK. Install with scripts/install-review-process.sh --harness all --target <repo>.

loop.caption: The Learning Loop
stations: Flags turn off without a deploy; someone is on call
Which layer should have caught it?
A lint rule, a skill line, an AGENTS.md line, or a bench case
change.diff and expected.json, path:line confirmed by an engineer, plus its clean sibling
A prompt, model or tool change is kept only if the score goes up
loop.figure: Every incident that review should have caught becomes a regression case.
loop.desc: Engraved wheel of five stations around a hub marked make bench and bench/corpus. An incident: flags turn off without a deploy and someone is on call. Every incident review asks which layer should have caught it. The answer becomes a lint rule, a skill line, an AGENTS.md line or a bench case. A bench case is change.diff and expected.json, with the path:line confirmed by an engineer, plus its clean sibling. The reviewer is scored against every case, and a prompt, model or tool change is kept only if the score goes up; then the layers meet the next change.

edge.caption: The Cloudflare Edge
edge.cliSub: deterministic, added lines only, path:line, values redacted
rows: Credential-looking value under [vars] in wrangler config
Turnstile secret or API token in a public env var
Access email header read without the JWT
workers_dev or preview_urls set to true
TLS, WAF or rate limits weakened in Terraform
items: Admin route with no Access app or auth check

edge.note: Reviews only: it never logs in to Cloudflare, calls the API or runs wrangler.
edge.figure: HIGH and CRITICAL block the merge; the Access header rule stays REVIEW, since the JWT check may live outside the diff.
edge.desc: Engraved plate of a gate through which a diff passes, between two ledgers. The CLI catches, deterministically, on added lines only, with path:line and redacted values: a credential-looking value under [vars] in wrangler config, CRITICAL, BLOCK; a Turnstile secret or API token in a public env var, CRITICAL, BLOCK; ssl = off in Terraform, HIGH, BLOCK; the Access email header read without the JWT, HIGH, REVIEW; workers_dev or preview_urls set to true, MEDIUM, REVIEW; TLS, WAF or rate limits weakened in Terraform, MEDIUM, REVIEW; open CORS in Worker code, MEDIUM, REVIEW. Reviewer only, since the diff rarely proves them: Turnstile without a server-side siteverify; an admin route with no Access app or auth check; WAF custom rules and bot management levels; AI Gateway bypassed and origin IP trust; Access and WAF state in the dashboard. It reviews only and never logs in to Cloudflare, calls the API or runs wrangler. OWASP IDs: A01:2021, A02:2021, A05:2021, API4:2023, ASVS 5.0 13.3.1. References: developers.cloudflare.com on Workers secrets, Access JWT validation and WAF.
